predicate: (t == 3) & isin(in_tok, [tok("v"), tok("u"), tok("3"), tok("j"), tok("t"), tok("b"), tok("e"), tok("k"), tok("c")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("n"), tok("2"), tok("p"), tok("t"), tok("1"), tok("j"), tok("o"), tok("q"), tok("k")]) & (n_seen([tok("n"), tok("2"), tok("p"), tok("t"), tok("1"), tok("j"), tok("o"), tok("q"), tok("k")]) >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely at position t=3 (97% of activations, 98.7% of mass; a few at t=2 and t=4). It never fires at the delimiter or during copying. Within t=3 it fires on only about 3% of steps, and which ones depends on a graded, roughly additive combination of tokens. The current input is v (strongest, 6.5x lift), u, 3, j, t, b, then e, k, c, and the earlier prefix contains n, 2, p, t, 1, j, o, q, k (prev_tok n or 2 is about 6x). Activation is largest when the input is v and the prefix has several n/2/p tokens (e.g. n p n [v], n 2 n [v]). It mostly fires on first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 93% of mass). It is not sensitive to L, digit count or first_tok beyond these. The boolean conjunction only approximates a graded token-weighted score, so precision and recall are both limited.
